title: The partition plan is announced
detail: Lord Mountbatten announced the plan to partition British India after concluding that a united transfer of power was no longer politically workable. Bengal and Punjab, both demographically mixed provinces, became central to the coming division.

title: The Indian Independence Act is passed
detail: The British Parliament passed the Indian Independence Act, creating the legal framework for two new dominions, India and Pakistan. In Bengal, this meant the province would be divided into West Bengal and East Bengal.

title: Power is transferred, but the border is still unknown
detail: Pakistan and India became independent on August 14 and 15. Yet many people in Bengal still did not know exactly where the final border would fall, deepening fear, uncertainty, and communal tension.

title: The Radcliffe Award divides Bengal
detail: The final boundary award was published two days after independence. Bengal was split along the Radcliffe Line into West Bengal in India and East Bengal in Pakistan, rupturing long-standing social and economic ties.

title: Mass displacement reshapes the region
detail: Partition triggered one of the largest forced migrations in modern history. Families were uprooted, communities fractured, and the experience of East Bengal under Pakistan set the background for later movements over language, democracy, and self-determination.
